title: Phase 7 · Stage 23: The reminder processor
summary: Simulate a background job day by day: a ReminderService that streams due-soon, overdue and final notices as an IAsyncEnumerable while the clock advances.

steps.title: A stream of results
body: Real libraries run a nightly job: *remind people two days before a book is due; tell them the day after it is overdue; send a final notice after a week.* Shelfwise cannot wait for real nights, so it **simulates** them: `advance 10` runs the job ten times, one simulated day at a time, which keeps every run deterministic.

The job produces reminders **as it goes**. `IAsyncEnumerable<T>` is a sequence whose items arrive asynchronously: the method `yield return`s each one as soon as it is known, and the caller consumes them with `await foreach`:
public async IAsyncEnumerable<Reminder> AdvanceAsync(int days, [EnumeratorCancellation] CancellationToken ct = default)
await Task.Yield();                       // a real job would await I/O here
if (KindFor(loan) is ReminderKind kind) yield return new Reminder(...);

`[EnumeratorCancellation]` (from `System.Runtime.CompilerServices`) wires a token passed to `WithCancellation(...)` into the iterator. Compared with returning a `List`, a stream lets the first reminder go out before the last day has been processed.

steps.explain: The iterator runs until each `yield return`, hands the value over, and resumes for the next one when `await foreach` asks.

steps.prompt: Match each day to the reminder it triggers (a loan due on the 16th).
steps.explain: Reminders fire on exact days, so each one is sent once: a relational switch on `DaysLate` picks the kind.

steps.prompt: Why does `ReminderService` loop over `library.Loans.Active().ToList()` instead of the live query?
options: It takes a snapshot, so changes to the loan list while reminders are produced cannot break the loop
Lists are faster to create than queries
steps.explain: The same deferred-execution lesson as `return-all` in stage 14: when the source may change while you iterate, materialise it first.

steps.title: Reminders while the clock moves
prompt: 1. Add `using System.Runtime.CompilerServices;` to the usings, and at the bottom:
record Reminder(DateOnly On, ReminderKind Kind, Loan Loan, string Title, string MemberName);

2. `ReminderService.AdvanceAsync(int days, [EnumeratorCancellation] CancellationToken ct = default)` returns `IAsyncEnumerable<Reminder>`. For each day: advance the library one day, `await Task.Yield()`, then for every active loan (in loan order) whose days late is exactly **-2**, **1** or **7**, yield a `DueSoon`, `Overdue` or `FinalNotice` reminder.
3. Create `var reminders = new ReminderService(library);` at the top. `advance <days>` becomes async: it prints one line per reminder as it streams in, then `Today is ...`:
2026-03-14 due soon: Dune is due 2026-03-16 (Grace Hopper)
2026-03-23 final notice: Dune is a week overdue (Grace Hopper)
Move the `advance` success arm into `HandleAsync` (keep the usage error in `Handle`) and remove the old `Advance(int)` helper.
